source_text: Interim, quod ad praesens negotium spectat, inculco liberum arbitrium nec ob aliud datum esse nec intellegi in alio posse, quam ut nec ad iustitiam nec ad iniquitatem captiva aliquis voluntate rapiatur.
pass_a_gloss: Meanwhile, what looks to the present business, I impress that free choice has been given not for another thing nor can be understood in another, than that no one be snatched with a captive will either to justice or to iniquity.

lemmas.lexica: LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will

pass_b_english: For now I stress what concerns the present question: free will was given for no other purpose, and can be understood in no other way, than that no one is dragged with a captive will either toward justice or toward injustice.

choices.why: Glossary default: arbitrium is the decision-power, not a later Augustinian/Reformation free-will locus.
Julian's forensic virtue that renders to each his own, without fraude or gratia (partiality).
rejected: righteousness (Pauline overlay unless the verse forces it)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
